title: VPC probe fallback conductor + Terraform sentry for graceful node isolation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a resilient, observable fallback layer for Private VPC health checks that isolates degraded nodes gracefully, automates safe Terraform-driven quarantines, and provides an operator-friendly runbook. The conductor coordinates detection signals (probe failures, KV cache stalls, packet loss) and triggers graduated remediation: traffic draining, tainting/policy update, Terraform isolation, and automated verification. This ticket covers design, Terraform module changes, a runbook, a small operator controller, and test harnesses.
acceptance_criteria: Conductor prototype receives probe failure events and applies a 3-stage mitigation (drain -> taint -> terraform-isolate) for simulated node failures
Terraform module `vpc-sentry` added with idempotent `isolate_node` and `rejoin_node` targets and covered by unit tests
Runbook documented with clear detection thresholds, manual override steps, and post-mortem checklist
Automated smoke tests validate traffic routing and KV cache integrity after isolation/rejoin
Dashboards show pre/post metrics for a synthetic failure and alert from Datadog/Grafana are generated as part of CI
runbook_steps: 1) Detect: Confirm repeated VPC probe failures (>3 probes in 2m) from at least 2 observers; correlate with node-heartbeat and CPU/network metrics
2) Triage: Identify node ID, AZ, and recent config changes (Terraform apply/upgrade) via infra-audit logs
3) Stage 1 - Drain: Use API to set route-weight=0 for the node and wait 60s for active connections to finish; monitor 200->5xx ratio and inflight token counts
4) Stage 2 - Taint: Add `redwood/private:tainted` tag in tag-store and mark node as `quarantine-candidate`; trigger canary traffic to verify degradation persists
5) Stage 3 - Terraform-isolate: Run `terraform apply -target=module.vpc_sentry.isolate_node[node_id]` in a sandbox workspace with plan output saved; persist plan ID and PR link
6) Verify: Run KV cache consistency check and smoke generation suite; ensure latency SLOs for remaining pool; run health check against isolated node to confirm improved cluster health
7) Rejoin: If stable for 30m, run `terraform apply -target=module.vpc_sentry.rejoin_node[node_id]` and follow the inverse flow (untag -> warm-up -> set route-weight back)
8) Post-mortem: Collect logs, attach Terraform plan/ops history, and create a retrospective with RCA and recommended mitigations
automation_playbooks: terraform-module:vpc-sentry@v0.3.1 - implements `isolate_node`/`rejoin_node` with state-lock safe hooks
k8s-controller:vpc-fallback-conductor@canary - listens to probe events and advances remediation stages; exposes dry-run mode
ops-scripts:bin/quarantine-audit.sh - gathers evidence and snapshots runbook steps to the incident ticket
ci-synthetic:test-harness/vpc-failure-suite - generates controlled packet loss and validates conductor path
test_plan: Unit: Terraform module tests (plan/apply with local backend mocked) to assert idempotency and no drift for isolate/rejoin
Integration: Canary run in staging with 3 nodes; force probe failure and assert conductor advances through stages and final cluster health matches target SLOs
E2E: Full lifecycle run including isolation -> rejoin -> post-mortem artifact generation; runbook steps executed by oncall in dry-run and live mode
Chaos: Inject network partitions (tc/netem) to validate that conductor does not quarantine nodes for transient blips
rollout_plan: Ship v0.1 to staging with feature-flag enabled in the controller (dry-run=true). Run 3 synthetic failures over a day and review metrics. Flip to dry-run=false for a 48h canary window restricted to non-critical customer accounts. If stable, enable in all regions with a 7d observation window and automated rollback if quarantine rate > 0.5% of nodes/day.
notes: Decision: Use Terraform for the final isolation step to ensure all network/iac changes are auditable and reversible via plan files
Tradeoff: A controller-level immediate isolate is faster but risks config drift; compromise is staged approach with controller triggering Terraform via an authenticated service account
Follow-ups: Add RBAC runbooks for auditors, and a synthetic monitor in Redwood Console to track quarantine frequency by customer tier
Related doc: RFC draft linked in Confluence at https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/VPC+Fallback+Conductor
